title: Private-Data Confidentiality at Network-Observer Scope (Non-Interference Hyperproperty)

cwe: CWE-200 Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
CWE-668 Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere

dascp.note: Formalizes the confidentiality-against-public-observer hyperproperty that C40-R aspirationally requires; the data-life-cycle aspects of C40-R (collection, retention, deletion procedures) are operational and stay out of BPO scope.
Provides the formal indistinguishability content C41-R points at; the identifier-level pseudonymization PROCESS (key custody, re-identification workflows) stays out of scope.

descriptions.semantic: An adversary with read-access to the network's public surface — block contents, emitted events, exposed storage slots, contract call returns — cannot distinguish between two valid system histories that agree on declared declassified outputs and on access-policy decisions but differ on any secret-classified data. Equivalently: the projection of an execution onto the public-observer view is a function of the declassified-public information only; the secret-classified data has no causal effect on what an outside observer sees, beyond what the system intentionally declassifies.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A relation between TWO executions of the same system that agree on public (Low) inputs, declassification predicates, and access-policy decisions, and differ only on secret (High) inputs. The property asserts the Low-projected traces coincide. This is a relational / 2-safety constraint over the trace-set semantics — not a property of any single execution — and so a hyperproperty in the Clarkson–Schneider sense.
descriptions.security: The cryptographic-and-systemic backbone of any privacy-preserving deployment: encrypted state, blinded commitments, mixed pools, off-chain compute with on-chain commitments. Failure is leakage through a side channel the engineer did not model — an exposed event, a public storage variable, a verifier callback whose timing or revert message is High-input-dependent, an oracle whose return value is High-input-correlated. Single-trace tools cannot detect such leaks even in principle.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Realized by partitioning inputs and outputs (and intermediate signals that escape via events/logs/calls) into High and Low labels under an information-flow policy with explicit declassification points (typically: 'the access-policy decision is Low'; 'the encrypted ciphertext is Low because hiding is delegated to the encryption layer'). Violations live in: implicit declassification through gas-cost differences, revert-reason content, event emission conditional on High, oracle inputs derived from High, or storage slots written conditional on High that are publicly readable.
descriptions.formal_verification: A 2-safety property. Verified by self-composition (instantiate the system twice with two High assignments agreeing on Low; assert Low-projections coincide) reduced to a safety check on the doubled system; by information-flow typing of the codebase (a well-typed program admits no High → Low flow except through declared declassification); by interactive theorem proving for the joint argument; and by cryptographic reduction for the encryption layer (e.g. IND-CPA hiding of ciphertexts at the Low boundary). It is a category error to claim this property on the basis of a single-trace tool: SMT on reachable states, single-execution symbolic execution, and single-run fuzzing CANNOT establish a hyperproperty, no matter how exhaustive.

formalization.signature: States S; transitions s --[a]--> s'; input partition I = I_Low ⊎ I_High; declassification predicate Δ : I_Low × I_High → Out_declassified; public-observer projection π_pub : Trace → ObsTrace (events, public storage, call returns, public timing); access-policy function ρ : I → Decision.
formalization.first_order_logic: Non-interference (declassification-bounded):  ∀ trace t1, t2 generated by the system from input pairs (i_L, i_H1), (i_L, i_H2) with i_L identical, Δ(i_L, i_H1) = Δ(i_L, i_H2), and ρ(i_L, i_H1) = ρ(i_L, i_H2)  →  π_pub(t1) = π_pub(t2).

temporal_logic.ltl: n/a — non-interference is relational and is NOT expressible by an LTL formula over single traces.

formalization.state_machine: Self-composed system S × S sharing i_L, ρ-output, and Δ-output; assert equality of π_pub projections across the two High assignments. The standard reduction of a 2-safety hyperproperty to a 1-safety property on the doubled system, suitable for ordinary safety checkers — but only when applied to the COMPOSED system, never the original.
formalization.type_theoretic: Information-flow typing: every variable, parameter, return, event field, storage slot, and external-call argument is labelled High or Low; the typing judgment forbids any flow from High to Low except through an annotated declassify(Δ) or declassify(ρ) operation. A well-typed program in this discipline satisfies the property by construction; verification reduces to type-checking plus an audit of the declassification points.
formalization.algebraic: The set of admissible behaviours is the equivalence class of public traces under the relation 'agrees on (i_L, Δ, ρ)'; the property asserts the equivalence class is a singleton at the public-observer projection.
formalization.hyperproperty: A 2-execution declassification-bounded non-interference property in the hypersafety class; reduced to safety by self-composition. Single-trace tools (SMT on individual reachable states, fuzzing, single-path symbolic execution) cannot establish this property.

relationships.note: Extends simulator-based ZK witness privacy from the proof-system boundary to the network-observer surface: the same indistinguishability discipline applied to public state, events, and calls rather than only to proof transcripts.

Circuit-level non-leakage (BPO:0073) composes with this system-level non-interference: a system whose circuits do not leak through public signals AND whose public surface beyond circuits does not leak through events/storage satisfies both.
Hiding properties of the encryption / commitment scheme used to render High values Low-observable (as ciphertexts) reduce to cryptographic hardness assumptions.

Full public auditability and full network-level confidentiality on the same data are in direct tension; selective disclosure (commitment + ZK proof of conformance) is the standard reconciliation, the same pattern BPO:0003 records against BPO:0072.

attack_surface.pattern: an event is emitted only when a High-input-dependent predicate holds (e.g. only when a balance is non-zero, only when a flag is set); the public observer learns the predicate value
attack_surface.notes: Either emit unconditionally with constant payload, emit a commitment + ZK proof, or do not emit.

attack_surface.pattern: a publicly readable storage slot is written conditional on a High value, or its post-state correlates with the High value (e.g. an incremented counter), so the observer reads off the High input
attack_surface.notes: Mask or commit; ensure post-state write pattern is independent of the High data flow.

attack_surface.pattern: gas consumption or call timing differs measurably across two equally-public traces because internal branching depends on High inputs
attack_surface.notes: Constant-time / constant-gas patterns for High-touching code paths; relevant especially for L2 sequencer-observable timing.

attack_surface.pattern: the revert reason string encodes a High-input-dependent error case, leaking which High value triggered the revert
attack_surface.notes: Use uniform revert reasons or revert-no-reason for High-input-conditioned reverts.

attack_surface.pattern: an oracle is queried with a High-dependent query, causing the oracle observer to learn the High input via the query pattern
attack_surface.notes: Query patterns must be either fixed or themselves commitments.

attack_surface.pattern: the policy admits more declassification than intended — e.g. ρ leaks more about i_H than the access decision requires
attack_surface.notes: Audit Δ and ρ for minimality.

metrics: count of High → Low flows annotated as declassify(Δ) vs unannotated (target: zero unannotated)
invariant_checkpoints: IFC type-check passes with zero unannotated High → Low flows
self-composition assertion holds on the doubled system
runtime_assertions: n/a — hyperproperties are not single-trace-observable at runtime; this property is static/relational

tools: Halmos / SMT over the doubled system
strategies.notes: Reduce 2-safety to 1-safety on S × S; assert public-observer projection equality across the two High assignments. The reduction is sound provided the composition preserves environment behaviour.
A well-typed program in the IFC discipline satisfies the property by construction; engineering cost is concentrated in annotating the declassification points and the public-observer model.
Reduce hiding of High data exposed as ciphertext to IND-CPA / IND-CCA of the underlying scheme; outside the reach of single-trace tools and SMT.

tools: SMT solvers on a single execution
strategies.notes: CANNOT establish a hyperproperty. They may find single-trace SAFETY violations en route (e.g. a crash) but cannot rule out information leakage across pairs of traces. Listed here only to mark them as inadmissible for this property class — including this line is the discipline of the catalogue.

testability: differential testing across paired High assignments with fixed (i_L, Δ, ρ): public observables coincide
IFC type-check produces zero unannotated High → Low flows
self-composition assertion holds for every release

runtime: uniform revert reasons / no-reason reverts on High-conditioned paths
no event emission gated by a High predicate
static: IFC labelling of every state variable, parameter, event field, return value, and external-call argument
annotated declassification points reviewed for minimality
design_patterns: commitment + ZK proof of conformance for any state otherwise High (selective disclosure)
uniform fixed-shape transactions regardless of High inputs
encrypted storage with separated key custody

assumptions.statement: The encryption / commitment scheme used to render High values Low-observable is hiding at the deployed security parameter.
Information-flow labelling is sound and complete across the audited code surface; every High → Low flow that exists is either annotated declassify(Δ) or rejected by the type-checker.
The Low (public-observer) model — what the adversary can read off the network — is precisely specified: which storage slots, events, call returns, gas signals, and timing signals are in-scope.

sources: Goguen & Meseguer, Security policies and security models (1982)
Barthe, D'Argenio, Rezk on self-composition for k-safety
EasyCrypt for the cryptographic reduction layer
provenance.notes: Authored to provide the network-observer-scope hyperproperty version of confidentiality. Refines BPO:0003 (simulator-based ZK at the proof boundary) to the broader public-observer surface; composes with BPO:0073 (circuit-level non-leakage). The single most important classification call in this catalogue: this is a 2-safety hyperproperty and any verification claim must respect that — the `Single-trace tools` strategy entry exists specifically to record their inadmissibility, not to license them.
